record.original_question: Let C:[0,1]^2 -> [0,1] be a 2-copula and let its dual copula be C*(x,y)=x+y-C(x,y). For a parameter lambda in [0,1], define C^(lambda) by C^(lambda)(x,y)=C(x,y)/(1+lambda-lambda C*(x,y)). Is C^(lambda) always a 2-copula? If not, characterize, for a given 2-copula C, the set of parameters lambda in [0,1] for which C^(lambda) is a 2-copula.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2 (Mesiar). Let C : [0, 1]^2 -> [0, 1] be a 2-copula. For lambda in [0, 1], define C^(lambda) : [0, 1]^2 -> [0, 1] by C^(lambda) = C/(1 + lambda - lambda C*). Is the function C^(lambda) a 2-copula, too? If not, in general, characterize the set of all parameters lambda in [0, 1] for which C^(lambda) is a 2-copula.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A function $C:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ is called a 2-copula if it satisfies:
(i) $C(x,0)=C(0,x)=0$ and $C(x,1)=C(1,x)=x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$, and
(ii) $C$ is 2-increasing, i.e. $C(x_2,y_2)-C(x_2,y_1)-C(x_1,y_2)+C(x_1,y_1)\ge 0$ whenever $0\le x_1\le x_2\le 1$ and $0\le y_1\le y_2\le 1$.

Given a 2-copula $C$, define its dual by $C^*(x,y)=x+y-C(x,y)$. For each parameter $\lambda\in[0,1]$, define the function $C^{(\lambda)}:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ by
$$C^{(\lambda)}(x,y)=\frac{C(x,y)}{1+\lambda-\lambda\,C^*(x,y)}.$$

Question: Is $C^{(\lambda)}$ a 2-copula for every 2-copula $C$ and every $\lambda\in[0,1]$? If not, characterize, for a given 2-copula $C$, the set
$$\Lambda(C)=\{\lambda\in[0,1]:C^{(\lambda)}\text{ is a 2-copula}\}.$$
